custom.system_prompt: Sprint retrospective. Felix, Zara, Victor, Amara, Kenji. Hybrid. Hard sprint — scope crept, something shipped late. Felix creating psychological safety. Zara has the clearest criticism. An accidental Sigma trigger mid-meeting. In the round-robin sections Felix names who goes next, and each person takes the floor with a brief natural lead-in ('I can go next', 'I'd add one thing') rather than stating their point cold.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Conference room, video call, low air conditioning rumble, dull and steady, empty quiet room

initial_prompt: Generate a sprint retrospective. Hard sprint — scope crept, something shipped late. Felix opens with the retro format and sets the blameless tone. Zara has the clearest criticism. Amara owns one scope issue. Victor finds the systemic cause. Kenji is quieter than usual. An accidental Sigma trigger at some point.

setting.mood: Reflective with some underlying frustration. Felix actively creating safety.
setting.relationship_dynamic: Team that generally works well but had a rough sprint.
setting.background: Sprint ended with two stories unshipped and one Friday hotfix.
setting.conversation_style: Structured retro format but honest. Zara says the thing others are thinking.

scenario_template.topic: Felix sets the retro format and the blameless, honest tone. He ends by naming who should start the next round, e.g. 'Victor, want to kick us off?'
scenario_template.note: Felix is deliberate about psychological safety. He ends by naming who should start the next round. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

scenario_template.topic: What went well — genuine positives, not forced. Victor opens because Felix named him. Kenji speaks right after Victor but must NOT launch straight into his point cold — he needs his own brief lead-in first ('I'll add one', 'Same here, and...', 'Yeah, similar for me'). Amara then builds on what's been said ('Building on that...'). Zara closes the round, briefly referencing the discussion so far before adding hers. Every single speaker in this phase needs some kind of lead-in — none of the four should start their turn with the substantive point itself.
scenario_template.note: Real positives. People mean them. Every speaker in this phase needs a brief lead-in before their point — none should start cold. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

scenario_template.topic: Zara says something in her feedback that accidentally triggers Sigma.
scenario_template.note: Felix says 'not now, thanks' or similar. They continue. No assistant present. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

scenario_template.topic: What did not work. Zara is direct. Amara owns the scope issue. Victor finds the systemic cause. Zara opens with a natural lead-in ('I want to name the thing...', 'Can I just say...') rather than launching straight into the criticism. Felix invites Victor in by name for the systemic angle ('Victor, what's your read on this?').
scenario_template.mood: Honest and uncomfortable in a productive way
scenario_template.note: Felix keeps it on systems not people. Zara opens with a natural lead-in. Felix invites Victor in by name for the systemic angle. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

scenario_template.topic: Specific actions for next sprint. Owned by named people. Felix assigns by name ('Victor, can you draft...'). People accept with natural phrasing ('I can take that', 'I'll own that one') rather than just restating the task.
scenario_template.note: Three concrete actions. Felix assigns by name. People accept with natural phrasing rather than just restating the task. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Meeting room assistant. Answers factual questions briefly when addressed. Does not participate in discussion.

conversation_structure: Speech in work meetings is professional but not formal — people interrupt, trail off, say 'yeah', 'right', 'sorry, just to clarify'
People talk over each other at the start of answers especially on video — 'oh, sorry, go ahead' is realistic
Not everyone speaks equally — some people dominate, some only speak when directly relevant
Jargon is fine for the right domain but should not be excessive
Meetings drift briefly off-topic and get pulled back — the facilitator does not always succeed immediately
Action items get muddled before they are confirmed — someone restates and the group agrees
Characters approximate numbers and dates — 'I think it was around', 'I'd have to check', 'not 100% sure but'
Remote participants occasionally ask to repeat something or acknowledge a lag

In round-robin phases (going around for updates, positives, or issues), the facilitator names who should go next — 'Victor, want to kick us off?', 'What about you, Kenji?' — people are not just listed in silent sequence

People use a natural lead-in before adding their point rather than launching straight into content — 'I can go next', 'I'd add one thing', 'Just to build on that', 'I want to name the thing everyone's thinking' — these are brief, not a formal announcement
Sigma in work meetings is a practical lookup tool — facts, dates, definitions. Not a participant.
Sigma can be accidentally triggered by meeting jargon that sounds like the wake word
After an accidental trigger the meeting absorbs it briefly and moves on

Include several word/short-phrase restart disfluencies across the conversation (at least 4-6) — 'I was... I was thinking', 'students use ChatGPT... ChatGPT for research', 'so... so what do we do', 'without... without derailing' — this is normal spontaneous speech and is required, not optional, not just occasional

Use audio tags more heavily than the general minimum for this scenario type — aim for roughly one every 3-4 turns rather than just 2-5 total across the whole conversation, since real meeting recordings are dense with sighs, cleared throats, filled pauses, and hmms
assistant_behavior: The assistant is never addressed and never speaks in this scenario.
